In 2026, prepare to GO TO HELL with Australia's first ever dedicated metal cruise 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃.
The boat will be rockin' and you'll wanna come knockin' next year, with 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 set to deliver an all-out, three-night floating heavy festival on the high seas! Promoted by 𝐂𝐇𝐎𝐎𝐒𝐄 𝐘𝐎𝐔𝐑 𝐂𝐑𝐔𝐈𝐒𝐄 and 𝐃𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐑𝐎𝐘 𝐀𝐋𝐋 𝐋𝐈𝐍𝐄𝐒 and bringing together the loudest bands and the wildest fans, 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 will transform a luxury cruise ship into the ultimate headbanger's paradise, departing from Sydney on Thursday 22 October in 2026 and, arriving back in Sydney on Sunday 25 October. With two uninterrupted days and three nights of festival programming and cruising, it'll be all hands-on deck for this once in a lifetime experience, also armed with a stacked lineup guaranteed to make even Captain Jack Sparrow weak at the knees.
Helming proceedings in 2026, 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 will be headlined by Aussie metal royalty, 𝐏𝐀𝐑𝐊𝐖𝐀𝐘 𝐃𝐑𝐈𝐕𝐄, along with performances from 𝐏𝐎𝐋𝐀𝐑𝐈𝐒, 𝐍𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐇𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐄, 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐁𝐔𝐓𝐓𝐄𝐑𝐅𝐋𝐘 𝐄𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐂𝐓, 𝐌𝐀𝐊𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐄𝐌 𝐒𝐔𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐑, 𝐈𝐍 𝐇𝐄𝐀𝐑𝐓𝐒 𝐖𝐀𝐊𝐄, 𝐁𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐄 𝐇𝐀𝐕𝐄𝐍, 𝐁𝐋𝐎𝐎𝐌, 𝐂𝐇𝐄𝐙, 𝐃𝐈𝐀𝐌𝐎𝐍𝐃 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐓𝐑𝐔𝐂𝐓, 𝐅𝐔𝐓𝐔𝐑𝐄 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐂, 𝐎𝐂𝐄𝐀𝐍 𝐒𝐋𝐄𝐄𝐏𝐄𝐑, 𝐑𝐄𝐋𝐈𝐐𝐀, 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐁𝐄𝐀𝐔𝐓𝐈𝐅𝐔𝐋 𝐌𝐎𝐍𝐔𝐌𝐄𝐍𝐓, 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐆𝐋𝐎𝐎𝐌 𝐈𝐍 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐂𝐎𝐑𝐍𝐄𝐑, 𝐓𝐎 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐆𝐑𝐀𝐕𝐄 and 𝐖𝐈𝐍𝐃𝐖𝐀𝐊𝐄𝐑.
And the festivities don't end there! With DJ sets, themed nights, artist-hosted experiences and non-stop metal-fuelled mayhem on the horizon for this once-in-a-lifetime experience, 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 will play home to 3,000 heavy music fans next October with something truly on offer for everyone on board. Combining the luxury of a cruise with riffs and moshpits galore, 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃's Carnival Splendor vessel will boast a custom-built main stage on the pool deck, an onboard fitness centre, Cloud 9 Spa and daily fitness classes - plus, your all-in-one ticket covers all entertainment, accommodation and food. Immerse yourself in gigs all day and night, party 'til all hours, or just take it all at your own pace, with multiple vantage points throughout three decks meaning you won't miss a thing. And take the headache out of sorting a designated driver - that's the captain's job!

One of Australia's most successful heavy music exports to date, 𝐏𝐀𝐑𝐊𝐖𝐀𝐘 𝐃𝐑𝐈𝐕𝐄 have spent the past two decades carving out a formidable reputation that doesn't merely live up to the hype; it sets the hype on fire (often literally). With seven full-length albums, three back-to-back #1 ARIA records, six albums certified Gold in Australia, multiple ARIA Award wins, millions of streams, international chart success, and thousands of live performances worldwide, the journey from teenage metal underdogs in Byron Bay to a bona fide global phenomenon is the stuff of heavy metal legend; and a 𝐏𝐀𝐑𝐊𝐖𝐀𝐘 𝐃𝐑𝐈𝐕𝐄 live show is a spectacle difficult to forget for those who have witnessed the fire and ferocity over the years.
Whether headlining the likes of Wacken, Good Things Festival in Australia and So What?! Festival, touring with Lamb of God, Soulfly and Killswitch Engage, or selling out some of their biggest shows to date with their 20 year anniversary Australian headline run last year, 𝐏𝐀𝐑𝐊𝐖𝐀𝐘 𝐃𝐑𝐈𝐕𝐄 are ravenous and riveting innovators in a live setting, not only set to make history in 2026 by headlining 𝐇𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃, but also in 2025 via their entirely sold out one-off live performance this June, performing with a full symphony orchestra against the backdrop of a fellow Australian and international icon: the Sydney Opera House.
Balancing relatability with an explosive blend of melodic metalcore, lush post rock, electronic flourishes and beyond, 𝐏𝐎𝐋𝐀𝐑𝐈𝐒 have faced and channelled life's angst, frustrations and despair through their music since first forming in 2012. In command of three studio albums, including their most recent outing Fatalism which debuted at #1 on the ARIA Charts, won Best Independent Heavy Album at the 2024 AIR Awards and was nominated for Best Hard Rock/Heavy Metal Album at the 2024 ARIA Music Awards, 𝐏𝐎𝐋𝐀𝐑𝐈𝐒 have also ticked off sold-out headline tours of Australia, huge runs across Europe, the UK and North America, and unforgettable festival appearances, including their debut at Knotfest Australia earlier this year, and supports with Bring Me The Horizon, While She Sleeps, Spiritbox and many more.
One of the most dynamic forces in the modern metalcore scene, 𝐍𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐇𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐄 effortlessly fuse heavy savagery with techno, drum and bass, and expansive arrangements. With multiple ARIA Award wins under their belts and six studio albums, including their #1 charting 2022 outing Obsidian, 𝐍𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐇𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐄's live show has seen them enamour both as headliners and/or supporting some of the giants of the scene, repeatedly praised for their energetic and enthralling stage presence and ever-expanding back catalogue. And repping the hard rock flag, 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐁𝐔𝐓𝐓𝐄𝐑𝐅𝐋𝐘 𝐄𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐂𝐓 ravenously returned to the airwaves and live scene since announcing their reunion back in 2017. With four studio albums, including the certified Gold Begins Here (2003), Imago (2006) and Final Conversation of Kings (2008), 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐁𝐔𝐓𝐓𝐄𝐑𝐅𝐋𝐘 𝐄𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐂𝐓 have also recently ticked

After a huge year of conquering the world, Melbourne metalcore standouts HEAVENSGATE are finally coming home with The Angel Hymns Australian Tour this October and November. Joined by Greyscale Records label mates Mélancolia and rising Sydney outfit Irken Armada, the five-date run will see HEAVENSGATE bring their internationally renowned live show back to Australian stages.
At the heart of HEAVENSGATE’s rise is their latest EP, A HEART IS A HEAVY BURDEN, a release that pooled the band's collective experiences into a sonically raging yet deeply personal take on modern metalcore that proved to resonate deeply with listeners. Building on the foundations laid by their 2022 debut EP AND ALL I LOVED, I LOVED ALONE, the record further cemented HEAVENSGATE as a vital new force in heavy music.
The Angel Hymns Australian Tour will land in between a North American run supporting 156/Silence and Aviana throughout September, followed by a European and UK tour alongside thrown, Counterparts and No Cure across November and December.
Joining HEAVENSGATE across Australia is Mélancolia, who have quickly established themselves as one of kind within Australia’s metal community. Since emerging in 2022, the band have released two critically acclaimed albums, HissThroughRottenTeeth and random.access.misery, via Greyscale Records and Nuclear Blast, and shared stages with Thy Art Is Murder, To The Grave, Fallujah, Cattle Decapitation, Ingested, Vulvodynia, Suffocation and more. Following multiple Australian tours and two European/UK runs, Mélancolia have well and truly made their mark beyond home soil.
Opening the shows will be Sydney metalcore five-piece Irken Armada, who have been steadily carving a name for themselves with a sound that nods to the genre’s mid-2000s heyday. Drawing influence from the likes of Underoath and Every Time I Die, the band blend nostalgia with a modern metalcore edge.

*** Northlane’s new album ‘Anemoia’ will be available worldwide on Friday 30 October. Available to pre-order on vinyl and CD here: https://au.northlaneband.com/ ***
Australian heavy music trailblazers, Northlane will embark on their biggest Australian headline this November with the Anemoia Tour joined by special guests After The Burial (usa), Cenobia + Above, Below.
Following on from their #1 album Obsidian (2022), Anemoia toys with the concept of feeling nostalgia for a time or place one has never known. This yearning opens up a dichotomy of darkness and light, where the sense of freedom of eras past buoys a carefree energy running through tracks like first single "Evian", while feelings of anger and despair come roaring back when the present day shatters the reverie, leading to some of Northlane’s heaviest moments since their first EP.
Across a career defined by seismic shifts, Northlane have stared down technological anxiety, alienation and collapse, channelling it into a highly influential body of work that is as expansive as it is confrontational. With the world in dire straits, it would have been easy for them to descend into the void on album number seven. Instead, they emerged from the studio with their most hopeful and human record yet.
More than 15 years into their career, Northlane continue to stand at the forefront of heavy music globally with a singular sound that shifts the genre’s landscape with every release. With multiple chart-topping albums, awards and over 500 million streams, the band has built a legacy defined by the restless pursuit of innovation. On Anemoia, they have not chosen between the worlds that shaped them - they have finally found where they meet.
Metalcore pioneers, After The Burial from Minneapolis will make their long awaited return back to Australia. Since their last visit down under back in 2019 when they supported Make Them Suffer, the band have been carving away with new material, Going on a hiatus for four years, the band returned with strength with a two track single 'Embrace The Inifinity' in 2023 and their latest offering with Hum From The Hollow in 2025.
Cenobia, the mysterious artist who bursted into the music scene back in 2025. As one of the major pioneers of nu metal, and one of the most successful bands in the scene of all time, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧’s signature collision of rap rock, grooves, searing riffs, angsty themes and larger than life performances has transcended the group from the late 90s breeding ground of MTV and teenage frustrations into enamouring a multi-generational fanbase with high octane party anthems and entertaining chaos decades since their formation. Exploding out of the gates with their debut full-length album, 1997’s 𝙏𝙝𝙧𝙚𝙚 𝘿𝙤𝙡𝙡𝙖𝙧 𝘽𝙞𝙡𝙡, 𝙔’𝙖𝙡𝙡, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧’s sophomore 1999 album 𝙎𝙞𝙜𝙣𝙞𝙛𝙞𝙘𝙖𝙣𝙩 𝙊𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙧 reached #1 on the US Billboard 200, ticked off two 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗠𝗬 Award Nominations, was certified 7 x Platinum, and spawned some of the band’s perennially adored singles, including 𝘉𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘬 𝘚𝘵𝘶𝘧𝘧 and 𝘕𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘪𝘦. Now with six studio albums under their belts, including 2000’s 𝘾𝙝𝙤𝙘𝙤𝙡𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙧𝙛𝙞𝙨𝙝 𝙖𝙣𝙙 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙃𝙤𝙩 𝘿𝙤𝙜 𝙁𝙡𝙖𝙫𝙤𝙧𝙚𝙙 𝙒𝙖𝙩𝙚𝙧 which set the record for the fastest-selling rock album of all time, and their most recent full-length venture, 2021’s 𝙎𝙏𝙄𝙇𝙇 𝙎𝙐𝘾𝙆𝙎, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 continue to blitz streaming charts to this very day, sell out international tours and headline powerhouse global festivals, including Download Festival earlier this year. 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 will make their return to Good Things Festival in 2026 as headliners following their unforgettable performances at the 2023 edition and selling out their headline sideshows in Brisbane and Melbourne. Believe the hype, there’s nothing quite like a 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 live show, and these will be monolithic performances to truly rattle the mainframe.
As one of the most culturally and commercially successful bands in rock, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have spent over two decades cultivating and evolving their status as pop punk legends. Now in command of over 10 billion streams worldwide, almost 2 billion views on YouTube, and an inescapable social media presence that bridges their longtime fans with a whole new generation, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have never been a band content to rest on their laurels. The group’s multi-platinum 2002 album 𝙉𝙤 𝙋𝙖𝙙𝙨, 𝙉𝙤 𝙃𝙚𝙡𝙢𝙚𝙩𝙨…𝙅𝙪𝙨𝙩 𝘽𝙖𝙡𝙡𝙨 introduced the world to smash singles like 𝘐’𝘥 𝘋𝘰 𝘈𝘯𝘺𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨, 𝘐’𝘮 𝘑𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘈 𝘒𝘪𝘥, 𝘈𝘥𝘥𝘪𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥 and 𝘗𝘦𝘳𝘧𝘦𝘤𝘵, while later hits spanning 𝘞𝘦𝘭𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘛𝘰 𝘔𝘺 𝘓𝘪𝘧𝘦, 𝘚𝘶𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘳 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘴𝘦, 𝘜𝘯𝘵𝘪𝘵𝘭𝘦𝘥 (𝘏𝘰𝘸 𝘊𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘏𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘯 𝘛𝘰 𝘔𝘦?) and more catapulted the Montreal-hailing quartet onto the main stages of Vans Warped Tour and When We Were Young, along with performances at the 2010 Winter Olympics, worldwide amphitheatre and arena tours with some of the scene’s biggest names, and massive headline treks along the way. Famous for their buoyant performances laden with pop punk anthems and infectious enthusiasm, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have also raised more than $3 million through their Simple Plan Foundation over the years. Recently celebrating their 25th anniversary in 2025, including a co-headline run with The Offspring down under, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 will once again wow Good Things Festival crowds in 2026 after their mesmerising appearances at the event in 2019.
The sonic equivalent of capturing lightning in a bottle, Canada’s 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫 solidified themselves as a household name in 2020 via their blistering breakout single 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘺 𝘙𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘳. Instantly capturing attention and exploding into a meteoric rise, the progressive heavy metal mainstays have notably never plateaued along the way, exceeding every expectation in 2021 with the release of their debut studio album 𝙀𝙩𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙖𝙡 𝘽𝙡𝙪𝙚, which debuted at #13 on the US Billboard 200, and ultimately rewrote the genre’s playbook in the process. With three 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗠𝗬 Award nominations under their belts for Best Metal Performance, including for 𝘑𝘢𝘥𝘦𝘥 in 2024, 𝘊𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘢𝘳 𝘋𝘰𝘰𝘳 in 2025 and 𝘚𝘰𝘧𝘵 𝘚𝘱𝘪𝘯𝘦 in 2026, 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫 remain one of the most influential acts in modern metal today; a fact echoed by the band’s equally beloved 2025 sophomore studio album 𝙏𝙨𝙪𝙣𝙖𝙢𝙞 𝙎𝙚𝙖, which hit #26 on the US Billboard 200, cracked the top 20 in the UK charts, reached #1 on the UK Indie charts and #12 on the Top German Album charts. A band simultaneously capable of boundless innovation, fearless reinvention and an unwavering connection to their burgeoning global audience, 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫’s live show boasts arena-level production, skull-crushing heaviness morphed alongside ethereal atmospherics, while immersing audiences head-first into the band’s unwavering energy and artistry that most recently was on display for audiences down under when the group made their debut Aussie performances at Knotfest Australia in 2023.
Also feeding the Good Things Festival matrix in 2026, Sydney’s 𝗣𝗢𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗦 are primed to stupefy with their blend of ferocity and melody, laced with blistering metalcore, post-rock and electronic influences. After relentless touring over the past few years, including supporting Linkin Park earlier this year for a massive national Australian arena run and supporting Electric Callboy in North America, 𝗣𝗢𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗦 will celebrate a range of hits with Good Things audiences later this year, including cuts from their most recent 𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗔 Award-nominated studio album 𝙁𝙖𝙩𝙖𝙡𝙞𝙨𝙢 which debuted at #1 on the 𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗔 Charts, secured triple j’s Feature Album upon release and won Best Independent Heavy Album at the 2024 𝗔𝗜𝗥 Awards.
